recent_commit_titles: fix(forge): install templates where rebar3 reads them
fix(forge): move template installer to repo root
sam-hyperbeam.rolling_context: Sam's visible HyperBEAM work continues to focus on making Forge and installable HyperBEAM functionality easier to use and safer to operate. Recent commits moved the Forge template installer to the repo root as `./install-template`, refreshed docs, and fixed template install paths so they land where `rebar3` actually reads them. PR #921 merged that setup cleanup, giving developers a simpler and more discoverable workflow from a HyperBEAM checkout. The latest merged PR #925 fixed the device loader so `load-remote-devices` is honored: local cache is checked, and gateway lookup only happens when explicitly enabled. That adds clearer operator control over remote fetching while preserving the path toward installable, shareable functionality. The durable theme is reduced friction plus fewer surprising defaults in the software layer that runs AO apps and processes.
sam-hyperbeam.current_phase: Forge usability and explicit device-loading controls
narrative_threads: HyperBEAM is making installable functionality easier for developers to create and share
operator controls are becoming more explicit around what nodes fetch and trust

recent_commit_titles: Port mystical devices to packaged HyperBEAM layout
test: add local paid whisper compliance flows
xylophonez-profile.rolling_context: xylophonez's visible public work continues to organize AO/HyperBEAM-adjacent experiments into packaged, testable, and documented forms. In `mystical.computer`, a large commit ported mystical devices to a packaged HyperBEAM layout and added service overlay examples for metered media, paid bundler, and whisper-style services. The same commit added bundler deployment examples, including Caddy and HyperBEAM config examples, making the service setup more reproducible. In `hyperbalance`, local paid whisper compliance flows were expanded with README/docs updates, revised examples, and a new transform example. The practical trajectory is repeatable developer workflows for complex service behavior, especially paid request and bundler-style patterns. This aligns with the broader AO ecosystem movement toward reusable layouts and examples that builders can run locally instead of reverse-engineering.
narrative_threads: experimental AO services are being organized into reusable project structures
paid request and bundler flows are getting clearer docs and local examples
